## What that was

| | Colonial Office List | India Office List |
|---|---|---|
| People | 27,526 | 19,400 |
| Dated career events | 180,470 | 124,694 |
| Events located to a Wikidata place | 131,343 | 80,238 |

36,431 arcs. 186 people who served in both services.

. . .

One historian, a coding agent, a few months. Ten years ago: five institutions, a grant, F-scores of 0.6.

::: notes
Trading Consequences one sentence. Then: the hour is how, and where I had to decide something.
:::

## Three questions

| | The question | The model does | You decide |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Structure** | What is a record here? | Proposes the fields, fills them for 100,000 entries | What counts as an event |
| **Clean** | One person or two? | Clusters, argues each case, keeps the evidence | Merge, keep apart, review |
| **Ground** | Which place, which person? | Retrieves candidates with evidence | Supported, unresolved, wrong |

. . .

**And the second half:** build, extract, **visualise, see, fix**, rerun.

## The source {.smaller}

> TRIMEN, HENRY, M.B. (Lond.), F.R.S., F.L.S. —Formerly lecturer on botany at St. Mary's Hospital, London, 1867 to 1875; was senior assistant to department of botany, British Museum, 1869 to 1879; director Royal Botanical Gardens, Ceylon, Feb., 1880; author of numerous works and papers on pure and applied botany.

> BALMER, F. E.—Dep. chief acctnt., G.P.O., E. Africa Prot., Mar., 1919; ch. acctnt., G.P.O., Kenya, Oct., 1919; ch. acctnt., Kenya-Uganda-Tanganyika post and tel. service, 1933; senr. dep. P.M.G., do., 1935.

85 volumes. 1,400–2,900 entries per edition. The same man in forty of them.

. . .

**Mark one up.** jimclifford.ca/trimen-workshop/annotate/ (or the paper).
Every position, place, year, honour. Three minutes.

# Structure

## The prompt is the decisions {.smaller}

> Extract ONLY what is printed; never invent or infer facts.
> **events:** one object per distinct posting. EXPLODE compound clauses into separate events.
> **place:** as printed. If the clause names no place, carry over the previous clause's place and set place_inherited=true.
> **birth_year:** only if explicitly printed. NEVER infer from the earliest career date.
> **honours:** with their award year if printed in parentheses; award-years are NOT career events.

Every rule exists because a run broke it.

Reference set: ~200 entries by a frontier model in session. The corpus: Qwen on a shared GPU, inside the script.

## Every tenth record, read against the source {.smaller}

| | |
|---|---|
| Sampled | 186 |
| Fully clean | 129 (69%) |
| Major error | 8 (about 3%) |

. . .

| Source | Record |
|---|---|
| "senr. dep. P.M.G., **do.**, 1935" | place: "do." |
| "BLAKELY, DONALD QUENTIN.—Clk., atty.-gen.'s off., B. Honduras, **Apl., 1898**." | birth_year: **1898**; event year: null; "officer" |
| "**KT. BACH.** (1920)" | honours: KT; BACH (1920) |

. . .

Systematic, not random. An expansion table, a forward-fill, a merge rule. **Not a bigger model.**

# Clean

## Forty editions, one person {.smaller}

> A missed link is recoverable; a false merge silently corrupts the record. **Ties resolve to no merge.**

1. Deterministic passes: 0 false merges on 543 hand-verified careers
2. Cluster the residue: shared forename + surname suffix, so OCR variants meet
3. A model argues each cluster from a dossier; the reason goes in a ledger (917 so far)
4. A 200-case silver standard, afterwards, to measure it

## Four clusters {.smaller}

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| ABERY, Joseph / CARBERY, Joseph | both M.B.C.M., both "1867 Ceylon asst. colonial surgeon" | **merge** |
| A'BECKETT, Thomas b. 1836 / BECKETT, Thomas Rumbold b. 1898 | a Victorian judge; a Nigerian telegraph engineer | keep apart |
| ABRAHAM, Henry Charles / GRAHAM, Charles Drummond | suffix "aham", forename Charles | keep apart |
| ABBOTT, Myles John / IBBOTT, John Thomas | Hong Kong 1936; Demerara 1860 | keep apart |

. . .

Easy with the dossier in front of you. The model's job was the dossier and the argument. **You decide** the one-shared-event cases.

# Ground

## Why {.smaller}

Every arc needs coordinates for "the Central Provinces", "British Guiana", "Jodhpur". Wikidata has the item, the coordinates, or the capital that has them. One query.

And: a historian of the Cape and a historian of Bombay who both ground to Q1800510 have joined their data without meeting.

. . .

**Two ways to get a QID.** Retrieve it, read the item, gate it. Or ask a chatbot.

## Live: the lookup

1. "Henry Trimen botanist Ceylon Peradeniya" → read the statements → **supported**
2. "Ferdinando Hamlyn Price" → Q123279571, alias Hamlyn, b. 1855, d. 1942, Tamil description only → **supported**, and the pipeline's gate had rejected it
3. "Elwood D'Arcy Tibbits Antigua" → nothing → **unresolved**, record the search

::: notes
WikidataMCP vector search. Saved results in outputs/ground-test/ if the network fails.
:::

## The control: Gemini 3.8 Flash, no tools {.smaller}

"Parse these bios and ground the places, schools and people to Wikidata ids where possible." Twenty entries.

| | |
|---|---|
| Person identifiers given | 16 |
| Correct | **0** |
| Not even a person (a plant, a patent, Thoth, a village, a reptile) | 6 |
| Within a few thousand of the right number | 7 |
| Place and school identifiers whose label matches | 43 of 142 |

. . .

Nyasaland → a disambiguation page. Straits Settlements → a Danish triathlete. Joseph Chamberlain → a Swiss footballer.

**It knew who. It did not know the number.** Nothing in the text tells you which ones resolve.

## Six Victorias {.smaller}

The Australian colony. The capital of British Columbia. An electoral district. A gaol in Hong Kong. A district in the Cape. A county in Mauritius. A town in the Seychelles.

. . .

Surface-keyed cache → one QID for everyone. Context resolver → per person. Six surfaces left ungrounded on purpose.

# The map finds the errors

## Three errors {.smaller}

| Seen | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| A premier of British Columbia with a seat in Melbourne | "Victoria" grounded once, by string | Per-person context resolver; also found the overrides had never applied |
| Union of South Africa at Harare: 960 events, 572 arcs | Containment match: "South Africa" ⊂ British South Africa Company | Five cache rows patched; containment guard; 100 pre-1910 events still ambiguous |
| Two Baluchistans | Colony under Q843 (Pakistan) and a second QID | One canonical row; duplicate folded |

. . .

Fix the **rule**, re-emit **both corpora**, rebuild the atlas, look at **everyone the rule touched**.

## What the map cannot find

False negatives. An ungrounded "Victoria" has no arc. A missed merge is two plausible short careers.

For those: silver standards. 200 hand-labelled cases, risky strata oversampled.
Rare surname + overlapping era: the judge's "different" verdicts were wrong **76%** of the time.

Write the reason. The reason is what becomes the rule.
Zoom: **Copy summary for chat**. Room: hands up when asked.

## Your own data {.smaller}

- **One question, one small sample, the page reachable.**
- **Build the view early.** It is your error detector.
- **Local identifiers first.** External ones after retrieval and review. **None from memory.**
- **Ground to the historical entity.** Resolve per person, not per string.
- **Ties resolve to no merge.**
- **Fix the rule, not the record; make the correction a test.**
- **Two kinds of model.** A frontier model writes the pipeline; a cheap one reads the collection inside it.

## Three questions

| | | You decide |
|---|---|---|
| **Structure** | What is a record here? | What counts as an event |
| **Clean** | One person or two? | Merge, keep apart, review |
| **Ground** | Which place, which person? | Supported, unresolved, wrong |
